50606542.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to human recombinant carbonic anhydrase 1 by isothermal titration calorimetry assay

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - ITC experiments: ITC experiments were performed using a VP-ITC instrument (Microcal, Inc., Northampton, USA) with 5–20 μM protein solution in the cell and 50–200 μM of the ligand solution in the syringe. A typical experiment consisted of 25–30 injections (10 μl each) within 3–4 min intervals. Variation of the time period between injections enabled the detection and elimination of possible kinetic effects that may distort the binding data. Experiments were carried out at 37 °C in a phosphate buffer containing 50 mM NaCl at pH 7.0 and with a final DMSO concentration between 0.5% and 2%.

original_paragraph.Results and Discussion - Binding studies: The binding affinities of indapamide-like benzenesulfonamides to recombinant human carbonic anhydrase isozymes I, II, VII, and XIII were determined by thermal shift assay and isothermal titration calorimetry. Figure 2 shows typical thermal shift assay data for inhibitor 3f binding to hCA II. Panel A shows fluorescence profiles of CA heat-induced denaturation, and Panel B shows the integrated compound dosing curves as a function of the concentration of added compound. Figure 3 shows typical ITC data for compound 3l binding to hCA II. Panel A shows a raw ITC data curve, and Panel B shows the integrated ITC curve. Fitting both TSA and ITC dosing curves yielded the binding constants for the binding of all tested compounds to the CAs. The observed dissociation constants for compounds 3a–o are listed in Table 1.
